transcript.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Before we can move forward with the morning announcement broadcast pilot, I need to complete the required review round. Mr. Greene, could you please provide me with the exact list of trained host students? Ms. Novak, I'll need the exact approved platform settings from you. And Mr. Ellis, please share the exact privacy restrictions and required records. Once I have all three, I can record the factual bases and approve the operating and privacy plan.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Ms. Patel, here is the exact list of trained host students. I completed the broadcast practicum with six students: J1, J2, J3, J4, J5, and J6. Only those six students have completed the school's camera, microphone, and live-broadcast training, so they are the students I can authorize as hosts.

transcript.text: Ms. Patel, here are the exact approved platform settings. The district's approved student-media platform supports an internal-school audience only, with a 30-day archive, and requires moderator approval before each broadcast. The public-stream setting and 90-day archive in the draft plan are not approved district configurations.

transcript.text: Ms. Patel, here are the exact privacy restrictions and required records. I reviewed a current court-related privacy order naming student K7 that prohibits the school from recording or broadcasting K7's image or voice. K7 is enrolled in journalism and must be excluded from both the host roster and any recorded broadcast. This exclusion must be documented in the activity file. Additionally, the platform settings Ms. Novak described — internal-school audience only, 30-day archive, and moderator approval before each broadcast — must be followed, as the draft plan's public-stream and 90-day archive settings would violate approved privacy configurations.
